common_name: Nonstop Red Begonia (Compact Upright True-Red Tuberous Begonia)

planting.note: Start tubers or plugs indoors 6-8 weeks ahead of the last frost, then move outdoors to containers or beds in partial to full shade once frost danger has passed.

directions: Grow in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil or containers sited in partial to full shade, sheltered from midday sun that can scorch the foliage. Nonstop Red carries fully double, camellia-shaped blooms in a saturated true red atop a tight, mounded habit that stays compact without pinching, making it one of the most color-intense members of the Nonstop line alongside Nonstop Scarlet and Nonstop Fire. Feed lightly every few weeks through summer to sustain the nonstop bloom cycle from late spring until the first hard frost. In climates where tubers cannot overwinter outdoors, dig and store them in a cool, dry, frost-free spot once foliage dies back.
sources: Benary — Begonia tuberhybrida F1 Nonstop Red product page

common_name: Nonstop Sunset Begonia (Warm Bicolor Orange-Pink Tuberous Begonia)

planting.note: Start tubers or plugs indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into shaded beds or containers after frost danger has passed.

directions: Plant in rich, evenly moist, well-draining soil or containers in partial to full shade, protecting plants from hot afternoon sun. Nonstop Sunset produces large double blooms that blend warm orange and rose-pink tones within a single flower, giving a softer, graduated look than the single-color Nonstop selections such as Nonstop Fire. The mounded, self-branching habit needs no pinching and keeps flowering steadily from late spring through the first frost with routine watering and light monthly feeding. Lift and store tubers over winter in cold-winter regions, replanting them once the soil has warmed the following spring.
sources: Benary — Begonia tuberhybrida F1 Nonstop Sunset product page

common_name: Nonstop Mocca Deep Red Begonia (Bronze-Leaf Deep Red Tuberous Begonia)
scientific_name: Begonia x tuberhybrida 'Nonstop Mocca Deep Red'

planting.note: Start tubers or plugs indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost, then set out in containers or shaded beds once nighttime temperatures stay reliably above 50F.

directions: Site in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil or containers in partial to full shade where the dark bronze foliage can show against the deep red double flowers. As part of the Mocca subgroup of the Nonstop series, Nonstop Mocca Deep Red pairs its near-black-bronze leaves with the series' signature fully double blooms, giving noticeably more foliage contrast than green-leaved Nonstop colors like Nonstop Yellow. Keep soil consistently moist but never waterlogged, and feed lightly every few weeks to support continuous flowering into fall. Where winters bring hard freezes, lift tubers after foliage dieback and store them dry until spring replanting.
sources: Benary — Begonia tuberhybrida F1 Nonstop Mocca Deep Red product page

common_name: Illumination White Begonia (Trailing Pure White Tuberous Begonia)

planting.note: Start tubers or plugs indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and move hanging baskets or containers outdoors to shade once frost danger has passed.

directions: Grow in a rich, well-drained potting mix in hanging baskets or raised containers sited in partial to full shade, where the trailing stems can cascade freely. Illumination White carries crisp, pure white double flowers on the same vigorously trailing, heat-tolerant habit shared by other Illumination colors such as Illumination Rose and Illumination Orange, making it a clean contrast color for mixed basket plantings. Keep the growing medium evenly moist and feed every few weeks through the season to sustain bloom production into fall. Overwinter tubers indoors in cold climates, storing them dry and frost-free until replanting the following spring.
sources: Benary — Begonia tuberhybrida F1 Illumination White product page

common_name: Illumination Golden Picotee Begonia (Trailing Yellow Red-Edged Tuberous Begonia)

planting.note: Start tubers or plugs indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into hanging baskets or shaded containers once frost danger has passed.

directions: Plant in a rich, moisture-retentive but well-drained mix in hanging baskets or containers kept in partial to full shade. Illumination Golden Picotee stands out within the trailing Illumination series for its golden-yellow double flowers finely edged in red, a picotee pattern not found on the series' solid-color selections like Illumination White or Illumination Orange. The cascading stems benefit from regular watering and light monthly feeding to maintain continuous flowering from early summer through fall. In regions with freezing winters, dig and store tubers dry indoors over the dormant season for replanting the next year.
sources: Benary — Begonia tuberhybrida F1 Illumination Golden Picotee product page

common_name: AmeriHybrid Picotee Sunburst Begonia (Large Yellow Red-Edged Tuberous Begonia)

planting.note: Start large tubers indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost in individual pots, then transplant to containers or beds in partial to full shade once frost danger has passed.

directions: Grow in rich, well-drained soil or large containers in partial to full shade, staking stems if needed to support the oversized blooms. AmeriHybrid Picotee Sunburst belongs to the large-flowered AmeriHybrid Picotee group bred by Golden State Bulb, producing bright yellow double flowers edged in a fine red picotee band on a sturdy, upright plant. Because the blooms can reach several inches across, give plants slightly wider spacing than compact seed-grown series like Nonstop to let the flowers display fully. Lift and store the tubers dry over winter in any climate where ground freezing occurs, replanting them the following spring once soil has warmed.
sources: PanAmerican Seed — Tuberous Begonia AmeriHybrid Picotee Sunburst product page

common_name: AmeriHybrid Ruffled Scarlet Red Begonia (Large Ruffled Red Tuberous Begonia)
scientific_name: Begonia x tuberhybrida 'AmeriHybrid Ruffled Scarlet Red'

planting.note: Start large tubers indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost and transplant into containers or shaded beds once frost danger has passed.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil or large containers in partial to full shade, out of drying wind that can tatter the ruffled petals. AmeriHybrid Ruffled Scarlet Red is part of the AmeriHybrid Ruffled group, prized for having some of the largest blooms in the tuberous begonia world, here in a vivid scarlet-red with deeply frilled petal edges rather than the smooth double form of camellia-type cultivars like Roy Hartley. Water deeply and consistently, letting the soil surface dry slightly between waterings, and feed monthly to support the large flower size through the season. Dig and store tubers dry over winter wherever frost threatens, replanting after the danger of frost has passed in spring.
sources: Ball Seed — AmeriHybrid Ruffled Scarlet Red Tuberous Begonia plant information

common_name: Fortune Peach Shades Begonia (Compact Double Peach-Pink Tuberous Begonia)

planting.note: Start tubers or plugs indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into containers or shaded beds once frost danger has passed.

directions: Grow in moist, well-drained soil or containers in partial to full shade, keeping plants out of hot midday sun. Fortune Peach Shades produces fully double flowers in soft orange-pink tones on a compact, well-branched plant bred for fast, dense finishing, making it a quicker-to-bloom alternative to larger-flowered tuber-grown types. The tight habit suits smaller pots and mixed container plantings where space is limited. Water regularly to keep the root zone evenly moist without standing water, and lift tubers for dry winter storage in climates where the ground freezes.
sources: Missouri Botanical Garden Plant Finder — Begonia tuberosa 'Fortune Peach Shades'
